thread:
support-esc: :rotating_light: multiple customer escalations coming in — several hosted API keys returning 502/504 and timeouts from eu-west-1 (looks concentrated in AZ eu-west-1a). Started ~1772104740 UTC, affecting both chat and generation endpoints. Customers report spikes in latency and intermittent gateway errors. Lots of repro steps included below. Posting sample error: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` and `504 Gateway Timeout` from our edge LB.

sre-oncall: I see same in monitoring — 5xx rate for hosted-api-prod in eu-west-1 spiking from 0.5% -> 18% over last 6m. Error budget alarms fired. Looking at instance-level: backends look healthy from kube liveness, but nginx edge shows upstream reset/read timeout.

netops: Can folks paste traceroutes / mtr from affected regions? Also checking transit provider alerts. Seeing increased TCP retransmits on a couple L3 hops.

support-esc: Customer provided repro curl: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rwd/text-1","prompt":"test"}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway` or connection reset after ~15s. They say retries to same region sometimes succeed.

customer-jd: (from customer) "we started seeing failures at 08:19 local (eu). Some requests succeed but most timeouts. We're throttling retries but it's impacting live feature rollouts — happy to provide pcaps if needed."

eng-runtime: No recent deploys to hosted edge in eu-west-1. Runtime dashboards show increased connection resets on the frontend proxy when talking to the regional inference pool. KV cache hit rates unchanged. Kernel errors nil.

infra-bot: Alert: hosted-api-eu-west-1-edge LB health alerts (rule: 5xx_rate > 5%) — 1772104862

netops: Pasted MTR summary from an affected client (redacted IP):
```
1. 10.0.0.1 - ok
2. transit-pop-05.example.net - 0% loss
3. transit-core-1.as12345 - 20% loss
4. provider-peering-2.as67890 - 35% loss
5. redwood-edge-eu-west-1a - 40% loss
```
This looks like packet loss across a provider path hitting our eu-west-1a edge nodes. Also seeing asymmetric latency to eu-west-1b nodes.

sre-oncall: Confirming: our edge metrics show increased request latency and dropped TLS handshakes specifically for sockets routed to eu-west-1a. eu-west-1b less affected but still degraded.

eng-runtime: Quick check — backend inference workers in eu-west-1a are still responding to healthz, but the proxy-to-backend TCP connections are getting RST/ERR on the edge. Could be upstream packet loss causing TLS session failures.

netops: Reached out to Transit Provider NOC — they are acknowledging packet loss on peering path and are investigating potential BGP flaps with one of their upstreams. AS numbers match the MTR. Provider suggests temporary reroute while they remediate.

cs-liz: Customer comms queued — drafting message to affected customers to advise we're investigating (no billing impact, not an auth issue). Will update with ETA for mitigation.

support-esc: Collected PCAP from affected edge node (anonymized) showing repeated TCP retransmits and client TLS timeouts. Also saw load balancer 502 logs: `upstream prematurely closed connection` spiking.

sre-oncall: Mitigation plan proposal: 1) divert new traffic from eu-west-1a -> eu-west-1b/secondary regions via smart-routing to avoid the affected POP; 2) increase retry/backoff to favor alternate AZs for in-flight clients; 3) work with provider for permanent fix. Can we trigger traffic shift?

eng-runtime: We can apply a traffic weight change at the global edge router to shift ~80% of new session establishment away from eu-west-1a within 2 minutes. Sticky sessions may still hit original nodes until reauth. We'll also bump global LB idle timeouts to force faster rehandshake to alternate edges.

netops: Executing route shift now — updating edge policy to deprioritize eu-west-1a POPs.

infra-bot: Action executed: edge-weight-update job 1772105027 — deprioritized eu-west-1a by 80%.

sre-oncall: Observing real-time metrics: 5xx rate in eu-west-1 dropped from 18% -> 3% over next 3 minutes. Latency normalizing for most customers. Some in-progress sessions still experiencing errors; we recommend customers retry.

customer-jd: Confirmed — our requests are succeeding again after ~2:30. Appreciate fast response.

netops: Provider NOC follow-up: they've identified an intermittent link flap at one of their aggregation switches causing packet loss to our POP. They are applying a config fix and monitoring. Estimated time to full restore -> 12-20 minutes.

eng-runtime: We rolled back the edge-weight to normal gradually after provider confirmed stabilization. Monitoring continuous — no reoccurrence after 15m.

sre-oncall: Current status: mitigated. Impact window ~08:19–08:34 UTC in eu-west-1a with residual effects until 08:50 UTC. Root cause: transit provider link flap causing packet loss/asymmetric routing to our eu-west-1a POPs, resulting in TLS handshake failures and upstream connection resets at edge LB leading to 502/504s.

cs-liz: Customer comms sent: apology + summary + guidance to retry and suggested failover patterns (regional retries). No billing credits planned — incident transient and provider-caused; will review on case-by-case.

support-esc: Logging post-incident repro steps for support teams: 1) collect curl sample, 2) request traceroute/mtr from customer, 3) ask for timestamps and region, 4) capture edge LB logs and PCAPs, 5) escalate to netops with AS hops.

netops: Post-incident followups: request provider postmortem, review peering diversity for eu-west-1 POPs, add additional health-check gating to avoid routing new sessions to POPs showing elevated TLS handshake failures.

eng-runtime: Action item: add more granular telemetry on TLS handshake duration and socket resets per POP. Also add automated short-circuit to shift traffic when handshake failure rate > 5% for 2m.

sre-oncall: I'll open an internal incident ticket and assign follow-ups. Marking incident as resolved for customer-facing channels. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Incident resolved marker applied at 1772105400.

support-esc: Thanks everyone. Will keep the ticket open until provider postmortem is shared and eng-runtime/netops confirm mitigations in place.
